sources.label: HTML Standard (WHATWG living standard) — the inline script element the cache applies to
V8 blog, "Code caching" (the bytecode-cache produce-then-consume mechanism the page's prose describes)

inventory.name: Inline script cache — bytecode caching for inline <script> blocks in HTML documents, with no API surface

syntax.rationale: There is no new grammar to learn, and the at-a-glance table is where the page states the developer-facing surface: it records 'API change: None — transparent performance optimisation', the status 'In developer trial (behind a flag)', and spells the one developer-visible control as code — the chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features enablement — beside the Spec row linking the HTML Standard with '(no new IDL)'. The markup being optimised is the unchanged inline script element, shown as code in the same table's Spec row and in full at #example-inline-script.

inputs.rationale: The input is the inline script's own source text: the example section shows a concrete inline script data island and then states 'The cache is keyed on script content. If the script text changes (e.g. personalised data embedded), the cache is invalidated and the script is recompiled.' The V8 blog documents the same produce/consume model, where cache data is produced from a script's compilation and attached to that source for later compilation. The page does not describe keying beyond script content; the live ChromeStatus summary adds a document network-isolation key to the SHA256 source hash — recorded as a carried disagreement in notes, not asserted here.

outputs.rationale: Nothing is returned to script: the at-a-glance table records 'API change: None — transparent performance optimisation', so there is no return value, callback, event or observable object for a caller. The effect is a browser-internal compilation-cache state (later loads of unchanged HTML skip inline script compilation), described in the page's own prose at #example-inline-script rather than exposed to script.

errors.rationale: There is no error or exception surface to document: the page names no throwing path and no failure state, and its only documented non-hit behaviour is silent — a changed script text invalidates the entry and 'the script is recompiled'. The V8 blog describes the same fallback as a cache miss (compile from scratch) rather than an error.

context.rationale: The at-a-glance table is the exposure context: status 'In developer trial (behind a flag)' in Chrome 149, the experimental-web-platform-features flag, no API change, the HTML Standard as the spec with no new IDL, the Blink component, and the ChromeStatus record. The feature applies to inline script blocks in HTML documents rather than to a new interface; the page's 'who benefits' table adds the page-level context (server-side-rendered pages, stable HTML, returning visitors).

lifecycle.rationale: The example section documents the state transitions with nothing to construct or tear down in script: the example's comment states the inline script 'is now cached after the first parse', the following paragraph documents the invalidation transition ('If the script text changes ... the cache is invalidated and the script is recompiled'), and the surrounding prose frames first load as compile and later loads as hit. The V8 blog documents the same produce-then-consume cycle for cache data.

examples.rationale: A complete <pre><code> example of an inline script (an HTML comment noting the script is cached after the first parse, and a JSON data island assigned to window.__INITIAL_DATA__ followed by an initApp call), which is exactly the shape the feature targets and the shape the page says requires no code changes.

compatibility.rationale: The browser support table lists Chrome '149 — developer trial (flag required)', Edge 'Tracking Chromium', and Firefox and Safari as 'N/A (implementation detail)'; the live ChromeStatus record agrees that Firefox and Safari views are 'N/A'. The table's Chrome status and its Edge row differ from / are absent from the live record — both sides are recorded in notes, neither adjudicated.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy surface for developers: the cache is browser-internal and not script-observable (no read, no key, no hit/miss signal), the feature adds no permission, origin or storage API, and the at-a-glance table's 'API change: None' plus the page's unchanged-markup framing mean nothing new is exposed to or reachable from page script. FLAGGED GAP, not silently claimed: the page makes no keying, isolation or storage statement at all, while the live ChromeStatus summary keys entries by SHA256 of the script source plus the document's network isolation key and the record's security/privacy reviews are 'Pending' — recorded in notes and in the unit report, not asserted on the page.

The page declares no IDL in its syntax region, so declaredSurfaceMembers() is empty and no outOfScope entries are needed. UNLINKED CITATION LABELS RESOLVED (AGENTS.md:91/103 ratchet): three citation spans carried the bare labels 'chromestatus summary' (twice, in why it exists and who benefits) and 'chromestatus' (browser support); each is now wrapped in its own , verified with curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' as HTTP 200 on 2026-10-07, and detectUnlinkedLabels() over the page now returns []. The other two page links (https://v8.dev/blog/code-caching, https://html.spec.whatwg.org) were already linked and were curl-verified 200 as well. CARRIED DISAGREEMENTS, BOTH SIDES REPORTED, NEITHER ADJUDICATED (ChromeStatus API fetched 2026-10-07): (1) CACHE KEYING AND REUSE SCOPE — the page says the cache is 'keyed on a hash of the script source, storing it alongside the HTML document's cache entry', that 'The cache is keyed on script content' and that only 'Pages that re-visit the same version of a page (same HTML content) now skip inline script compilation on subsequent loads' (it also lists 'Pages where the HTML changes on every load ... see less benefit'), whereas the live ChromeStatus summary for 5132993816559616 says entries 'are keyed by a cryptographic hash (SHA256) of the script source and the document's network isolation key' and that the browser reuses compiled execution data 'across different pages and sessions on the same site'. The two descriptions differ on both the key (source hash only vs source hash + document network-isolation key) and the reach (document-bound revisits vs cross-page/cross-session on one site). Relevant context, recorded rather than used to break the tie: the page's document-bound framing matches the older V8 post that carries the label the page links (https://v8.dev/blog/code-caching-for-devs, 2019: inline caches 'become dependent on the entire HTML document not changing, and are not shared between pages'), i.e. the page may be describing the pre-149 attached-to-the-document cache while ChromeStatus describes what 149 changes. (2) BLINK COMPONENT — the page's at-a-glance table says 'Blink>JavaScript>Compiler'; the live record's blink_components and browsers.chrome.blink_components are ['Blink>HTML>Script']. (3) STATUS/OPT-IN — the page says 'In developer trial (behind a flag)' with enablement via chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features and '149 — developer trial (flag required)'; the live record reports browsers.chrome.status.text 'Proposed' (milestone_str 'Proposed'), browsers.chrome.flag false, intent_stage 'None', feature_type 'No developer-visible change', is_released false, while active stage 5160591615459328 is the dev-trial stage (stage_type 330, desktop_first/android_first 149) and the record carries flag_name 'inline-script-cache' and finch_name 'InlineScriptCache'. A dev trial riding the generic experimental flag is consistent with flag:false, as in the B1 pilot, but the record names a dedicated flag and does not carry the generic one, and the page does not disclose the record's current status; recorded, not resolved. (4) V8 BLOG LABEL vs HREF — the see-also label reads 'V8 blog: Code caching for JavaScript developers' (the title of https://v8.dev/blog/code-caching-for-devs, 2019) while its href points at https://v8.dev/blog/code-caching ('Code caching', 2015, V8 4.2). Both URLs are live (HTTP 200); the linked 2015 post documents the bytecode-cache produce/consume mechanism, and the post whose title the label names is the one whose 'Avoid inline scripts' section describes the document-attached inline cache behind the page's prose. The label is linked, so the citation ratchet is satisfied; the mismatch is reported here for the implementer, not fixed. (5) UNSUPPORTED SPECIFIC — the page states external scripts 'have benefited from bytecode caching since Chrome 66'; none of the sources linked from the page states Chrome 66 (the linked 2015 V8 post records code caching since V8 4.2 with a "seen at least twice" production heuristic), and I did not find a page-linked source for that number, so it is recorded as unverified rather than corrected. Consistent, not a disagreement: 'Edge — Tracking Chromium' has no counterpart field in the ChromeStatus record (the record's browsers object carries chrome, ff, safari, webdev), so it is a general Chromium-follows statement rather than a record value. PAGE TEXT LEFT UNTOUCHED, as the B-unit scope requires; the page's remaining links — the see-also chrome-platform-showcase demo https://chrome-platform-showcase.paulkinlan-ea.deno.net/v149/inline-script-cache/ and the byline https://paul.kinlan.me/ — were curl-verified HTTP 200 on 2026-10-07 as well, and no live-demo behavioural divergence was assessed further in this unit.
